headline: Chips and Gas Producers Lead a Selective Monday Rally
body_html:
Chips set the tone for Monday's session. Semiconductors climbed 2.2%, the best showing among the eight groups we track, and 337 of the 544 stocks in our universe finished higher against 202 that fell. The strength reached well beyond the chipmakers themselves: Arm Holdings added 6.19%, Coherent rose 5.83%, Everpure gained 6.49% and Vicor jumped 10.64%, while Comfort Systems advanced 7.18%. The common thread was companies tied to building out computing capacity.

Energy was the second-strongest group, up 1.19%, and it produced the day's standout mover. Range Resources surged 17.66%, the largest gain on our board. Headlines offered a busy backdrop, from talk of a possible renewed Iran conflict to hopes for diplomacy that lifted most Gulf bourses, though none of that explains one stock's leap by itself. Industrials added 0.64%.

Homebuilders were the lone group in the red, off 0.94%, as commentary about mortgage rates holding above 7% circulated. Healthcare, materials, software and consumer names barely moved, ranging from 0.02% to 0.23%. Even so, the tape had cracks: Fair Isaac tumbled 13.15% and Amkor fell 6.34% despite the chip rally. Leadership was narrow and specific. Tuesday, October 27, will show whether it holds.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac Takes the Day's Biggest Hit
briefs.body: Fair Isaac dropped 13.15%, the steepest decline on our board and well out of step with a market where most stocks rose. The financial-data name stood apart from the broader tape, which suggests the move was about the company itself rather than any wider shift in sentiment.

briefs.headline: Amkor Slips Even as Chips Rally
briefs.body: Chip-packaging firm Amkor Technology fell 6.34% while the semiconductor group as a whole gained 2.2%. The split is a reminder that a strong sector day does not lift every name, and that investors were picking among suppliers to the industry rather than buying it wholesale.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Stand Alone on the Downside
briefs.body: Homebuilders slid 0.94%, the only one of our eight groups to finish lower. Commentary circulating Monday argued that mortgage rates above 7% have become the new normal, a backdrop that tends to weigh on companies reliant on buyers who need financing.

briefs.headline: Gulf Markets Mostly Rebound on Diplomacy Hopes
briefs.body: Most Gulf stock markets recovered on hopes that diplomacy with Iran could ease tensions. Egypt was the exception, slipping ahead of a vote on military support for Saudi Arabia after escalating Houthi attacks. The split showed how unevenly regional investors were reading the risks.

briefs.headline: Refiner Merger Collapses as Valuations Climb
briefs.body: Spanish and Portuguese energy groups Galp and Moeve have abandoned plans to combine their downstream operations. Reports tied the decision to the conflict involving Iran, which has lifted what refineries are considered worth and apparently changed the appeal of a deal.

briefs.headline: London Braces for a Cautious Budget
briefs.body: Britain's chancellor is expected to deliver a careful budget, with an eye on how financial markets will react. The tone points to a government wary of unsettling investors, and traders will be watching for any hint of surprises in the details.
